label: lem:global additive rigidity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:global additive rigidity}
If $V_c$ is Hodge--Tate at every place $v\mid\ell$, then $c=0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $v\mid\ell$.
The representation $V_c|_{G_{F_v}}$ is an extension of the trivial representation ${\mathds Q}_\ell$ by itself.
Since it is Hodge--Tate by hypothesis, additivity of the multiplicities of Hodge--Tate weights in short exact sequences shows that all its weights are zero.
Applying Sen's theorem \cite[Corollary~1]{Sen1973a} over the completion of the maximal unramified extension of $F_v$ shows that $I_v$ has finite image on $V_c$.
Thus $c(I_v)$ is finite and hence zero, since the additive group of ${\mathds Q}_{\ell}$ is torsion-free.

Now let $v\nmid\ell$, and let $p$ be the residue characteristic of $F_v$.
Since $c$ is additive, its restriction to $G_{F_v}$ factors through the abelianization.
Local class field theory therefore identifies $c(I_v)$ with the image of a continuous homomorphism $\mathcal{O}_{F_v}^{\times}\to {\mathds Q}_{\ell}$.
The group $\mathcal{O}_{F_v}^{\times}$ has an open pro-$p$ subgroup, whereas every compact subgroup of ${\mathds Q}_{\ell}$ is pro-$\ell$.
Since $p\ne\ell$, this open subgroup has trivial image, so $c(I_v)$ is again finite and hence zero.

We have shown that $c$ is unramified at every finite place of $F$.
Since the target of $c$ is abelian, global class field theory makes $c$ factor through the narrow class group of $F$, which is finite.
As ${\mathds Q}_{\ell}$ has no nonzero finite subgroup, we conclude that $c=0$.
head: environment

label: prop:no-unipotent quotient for global representation
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:no-unipotent quotient for global representation}
Let $ \rho \colon G_F\to \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(V) $ be a continuous finite-dimensional representation over ${\mathds Q}_\ell$.
Suppose that $V$ is Hodge--Tate at every place $v \mid \ell$.
If $G$ is the algebraic monodromy group of $V$, then $G^\circ$ has no nontrivial unipotent algebraic quotient.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By replacing $F$ by a finite extension, we may assume that $G=G^\circ$.
Let $c\colon G\to\mathbb{G}_a$ be an algebraic homomorphism and consider the two-dimensional representation $V_c$ of $G$ as above.
By \cite[Theorem~4.14]{Milne17}, $V_c$ is a subquotient of a finite direct sum of tensor products of $V$ and its dual $V^\vee$, and hence $V_c$ is Hodge--Tate at every place $v\mid\ell$.
It then follows from \Cref{lem:global additive rigidity} that $c$ is trivial.
A nontrivial connected unipotent quotient of $G$ would admit $\mathbb{G}_a$ as a quotient \cite[Propositions~14.21 and~14.22]{Milne17}, contradicting what we have just proved.
head: environment

label: thm:no-unipotent quotient for geometric representation
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:no-unipotent quotient for geometric representation}
Let $F$ be a finitely generated field over ${\mathds Q}$ and let $X$ be a smooth proper variety over $F$.
Let $\mathrm{G}_\ell(X)$ be the algebraic monodromy group of the representation
\[
 \rho_\ell \colon G_F\longrightarrow \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^\bullet_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline F},{\mathds Q}_\ell)).
\]
Then $\mathrm{G}_\ell(X)^\circ$ has no nontrivial unipotent algebraic quotient.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the standard specialization argument using Hilbert irreducibility \cite[Section~10.6]{SerreMW1997} (see also \cite[Section~5]{CadoretMotivated2013}), it suffices to treat the case where $F$ is a number field.
In this case, $H^\bullet_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline F},{\mathds Q}_\ell)$ is Hodge--Tate at every place above $\ell$ by \cite{Faltings88,Tsuji}.
The assertion therefore follows from \Cref{prop:no-unipotent quotient for global representation}.
head: environment

label: thm: semisimple MT conjecture
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: semisimple MT conjecture}
Under the comparison isomorphism
\[
H^\bullet_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline F},{\mathds Q}_\ell)
\simeq H^\bullet_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q})\otimes_{\mathds Q}{\mathds Q}_\ell,
\]
we have $\operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})_{{\mathds Q}_\ell}\subset\mathrm{G}_\ell(X)^\circ$.
Moreover, $\mathrm{R}_{u,\ell}$ commutes with $\operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})_{{\mathds Q}_\ell}$, and multiplication induces a canonical decomposition
\begin{equation}\label{eq:semisimple MTC}
\mathrm{G}_\ell(X)^\circ
=
\operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})_{{\mathds Q}_\ell}\times\mathrm{R}_{u,\ell}.
\end{equation}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: See \cite[Lemma~3.3.2 and Proposition~5.2.2]{TZ26}.
head: environment

label: thm: MT conjecture
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Projection onto the second factor in \eqref{eq:semisimple MTC} makes $\mathrm{R}_{u,\ell}$ a unipotent algebraic quotient of $\mathrm{G}_\ell(X)^\circ$.
Thus $\mathrm{R}_{u,\ell}=1$ by \Cref{thm:no-unipotent quotient for geometric representation}, which proves \eqref{eq: MT conjecture}.
For every $i$, the degree-$i$ projection satisfies $p_i(\mathrm{G}_\ell(X)^\circ)=\mathrm{G}_{\ell,i}(X)^\circ$.
Applying $p_i$ to \eqref{eq: MT conjecture} therefore gives
\[
\mathrm{G}_{\ell,i}(X)^\circ
=p_i(\operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})_{{\mathds Q}_\ell})
=\operatorname{MT}_i(X_{\mathds C})_{{\mathds Q}_\ell},
\]
which proves $\textup{(MTC)}_i$ in every degree.
Reductivity of Mumford--Tate groups then implies semisimplicity by \cite[Corollary~22.43]{Milne17}.

label: Example: WD rep ell adic case
title: Example
body_md:
\label{Example: WD rep ell adic case}
Assume that $\ell \neq p$.
Let $ \phi \colon G_K \to \mathbf{G}({\mathds Q}_\ell) $ be a continuous homomorphism.
We fix an isomorphism ${\mathds Z}_\ell(1) \simeq {\mathds Z}_\ell$ (as ${\mathds Z}_\ell$-modules).
Let $t_\ell\colon I_K \to {\mathds Z}_\ell(1) \simeq {\mathds Z}_\ell$ be the usual maximal pro-$\ell$ quotient.
By Grothendieck's monodromy theorem, there exists a unique nilpotent element $N \in \mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits(\mathbf{G})$ such that $\phi(\sigma)=\exp(t_\ell(\sigma)N)$ for all elements $\sigma$ of some open subgroup of $I_K$.
We fix a geometric Frobenius lift $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q \in W_K$.
We define $r \colon W_K \to \mathbf{G}({\mathds Q}_\ell)$ by $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits^n_q \sigma \mapsto \phi(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits^n_q \sigma)\exp(-t_\ell(\sigma)N)$.
After passing to $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$, we obtain the $\mathbf{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representation $\rho(\phi) \coloneqq (r,N)$ of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$, whose equivalence class is independent of the choices of ${\mathds Z}_\ell(1) \simeq {\mathds Z}_\ell$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q$ (see \cite[Lemma~8.4.3 and Variant~8.11]{Deligne73}).
head: environment
labels: Example: WD rep ell adic case

label: Example: WD rep p adic case
title: Example
body_md:
\label{Example: WD rep p adic case}
Assume that $\ell =p$.
Let $ \phi \colon G_K \to \mathbf{G}({\mathds Q}_\ell) $ be a continuous homomorphism.
We assume that $\phi$ is potentially semistable, that is, for every finite-dimensional representation $V \in \mathrm{Rep}_{{\mathds Q}_p}(\mathbf{G})$, the induced $G_K$-action on $V$ is potentially semistable\footnote{It suffices to check this condition for one faithful representation; see \cite[Lemma 2.8]{IM20} for example.}
Let $K_0$ be the maximal unramified subfield of $K$ and $K^{\operatorname{ur}}_0 \subset \overline{K}$ the maximal unramified extension of $K_0$.
Every $V \in \mathrm{Rep}_{{\mathds Q}_p}(\mathbf{G})$ gives rise to the $(\varphi,N)$-module
\[
D_{\operatorname{pst}}(V) \coloneqq \varinjlim_{L}(V\otimes_{{\mathds Q}_p} B_{\operatorname{st}})^{G_L}
\]
over $K^{\operatorname{ur}}_0$, where $L \subset \overline{K}$ runs over all finite Galois extensions of $K$.
We choose an embedding $\tau \colon K^{\operatorname{ur}}_0 \hookrightarrow \overline{{\mathds Q}}_p$ (over ${\mathds Q}_p$).
The construction $ V \mapsto D_{\operatorname{pst}}(V) \otimes_{K^{\operatorname{ur}}_0} \overline{{\mathds Q}}_p $ induces an exact tensor functor $\omega' \colon \mathrm{Rep}_{{\mathds Q}_p}(\mathbf{G}) \to \mathop{\mathrm{Vect}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_p}$, where $\mathop{\mathrm{Vect}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_p}$ is the category of finite-dimensional $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_p$-vector spaces.
Let $\omega \colon \mathrm{Rep}_{{\mathds Q}_p}(\mathbf{G}) \to \mathop{\mathrm{Vect}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_p}$ be the canonical fiber functor $V \mapsto V_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_p}$.
By Tannakian formalism, there exists an isomorphism $\omega \simeq \omega'$ of tensor functors, and this induces an isomorphism $\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_p} \simeq \underline{\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}\nolimits}^{\otimes}(\omega')$.
For each $V \in \mathrm{Rep}_{{\mathds Q}_p}(\mathbf{G})$, the Weil group $W_K$ acts on $D_{\operatorname{pst}}(V)$ by
\[
  \sigma \otimes \sigma \varphi^{-\alpha(\sigma)[{\mathds F}_q:{\mathds F}_p]},\quad \forall\sigma \in W_K\,.
\]
This action and the monodromy operators on the $(\varphi,N)$-modules are compatible with tensor operations in $V$.
Hence, via the chosen tensor isomorphism $\omega \simeq \omega'$, they define a continuous homomorphism $ r\colon W_K\to \mathbf{G}(\overline{{\mathds Q}}_p) $ together with an element $ N\in \mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits(\mathbf{G})_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_p}$ such that $\rho(\phi) \coloneqq (r,N)$ is a $\mathbf{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representation of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_p$.
The equivalence class of $\rho(\phi)$ is independent of the choices of $\tau$ and $\omega \simeq \omega'$.

label: Example: integral Weil-Deligne construction
title: Example
body_md:
\label{Example: integral Weil-Deligne construction}
Assume that $\ell\neq p$.
Let
\[
\mathcal{G}\hookrightarrow\prod_i\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(V_i)
\]
be a reductive closed subgroup scheme over ${\mathds Z}_\ell$, where $\prod_i\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(V_i)$ is a finite product and each $V_i$ is a finite free ${\mathds Z}_\ell$-module of rank $n_i$.
Assume that $\ell>\max_i n_i$.
Let $ \phi\colon G_K\to\mathcal G({\mathds Z}_\ell) $ be a continuous homomorphism, and let $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ denote the integral closure of ${\mathds Z}_\ell$ in $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$.
We choose an isomorphism ${\mathds Z}_\ell(1)\simeq{\mathds Z}_\ell$ and a geometric Frobenius lift $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q\in W_K$.
Let $(r, N)$ be the $\mathcal G$-valued Weil--Deligne representation of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$ associated with the generic fiber of $\phi$ using our fixed choices ${\mathds Z}_\ell(1)\simeq{\mathds Z}_\ell$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q$.
We shall show that $r \colon W_K \to \mathcal G(\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell)$ takes values in $\mathcal G(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$ and $N$ belongs to $\mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits(\mathcal G)_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$.

Choose $\sigma\in I_K$ with $t_\ell(\sigma)=1$, and write $g_i$ and $N_i$ for the actions of $\phi(\sigma)$ and $N$ on $V_i\otimes_{{\mathds Z}_\ell}\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$.
The eigenvalues of $g_i$ are roots of unity, and its unipotent part is $\exp(N_i)$.
If an eigenvalue has order divisible by $\ell$, then the inequality $n_i<\ell$ forces the characteristic polynomial of $g_i$ to be irreducible over ${\mathds Q}_\ell$.
Thus $g_i$ is semisimple and $N_i=0$.
If the semisimple part of $g_i$ has order $e_i$ prime to $\ell$, then $g_i^{e_i}=\exp(e_iN_i)$ is unipotent.
This, together with $(g_i^{e_i}-1)^{n_i}=0$ and $n_i<\ell$, implies that
\[
N_i=\frac{1}{e_i}\log(g_i^{e_i})
=\frac{1}{e_i}\sum_{j=1}^{n_i-1}
\frac{(-1)^{j+1}}{j}(g_i^{e_i}-1)^j
\in\mathop{\mathrm{End}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}(V_i\otimes_{{\mathds Z}_\ell}\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell).
\]
Similarly, $\exp(tN_i)$ is defined over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ for every $t\in{\mathds Z}_\ell$.
Since $\mathcal G$ is closed in $\prod_i\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(V_i)$, it follows that
\[
N\in\mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits(\mathcal G)_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell},
\quad
r(W_K)\subset\mathcal G(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell),
\]
as desired.
The resulting $\mathcal G$-valued Weil--Deligne representation of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ is also denoted by $\rho(\phi)=(r, N)$.
In contrast to the rational case, its equivalence class may depend on the choices of ${\mathds Z}_\ell(1)\simeq{\mathds Z}_\ell$ and $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q$.
The following proposition shows that it is independent of these choices under an additional hypothesis.
head: environment

label: Proposition: independence of integral WD construction
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Proposition: independence of integral WD construction}
Keep the notation and assumptions of \Cref{Example: integral Weil-Deligne construction}.
Assume that $\ell\nmid(q-1)$ and that there exists a geometric Frobenius lift $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q\in W_K$ such that, for every $i$, any two distinct eigenvalues $a, b$ of $\phi(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q)$ on $V_i\otimes_{{\mathds Z}_\ell}\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$ satisfy $a-b\in \overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell^\times$.
Then the equivalence class of $\rho(\phi)$ over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ is independent of the choices of ${\mathds Z}_\ell(1)\simeq{\mathds Z}_\ell$ and the geometric Frobenius lift.
head: environment
labels: Proposition: independence of integral WD construction

title: Proof
body_md:
We follow the arguments of \cite[Lemma~8.4.3 and Variant~8.11]{Deligne73}.
If $N=0$, then $r=\phi|_{W_K}$, and the assertion is immediate.
We henceforth assume that $N\neq0$.

Since $q-1\in{\mathds Z}_\ell^\times$, the same argument as in \cite[Lemma~8.4.3]{Deligne73} shows that, with the identification ${\mathds Z}_\ell(1)\simeq{\mathds Z}_\ell$ fixed, changing the geometric Frobenius lift yields an equivalent $\mathcal{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representation over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.

Changing the identification ${\mathds Z}_\ell(1)\simeq{\mathds Z}_\ell$ leaves $r$ unchanged and replaces $N$ by $aN$ for some $a\in{\mathds Z}_\ell^\times$.
Let $x=\phi(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q)$ and let $x_s$ be its semisimple part.
By the assumption, the eigenspace decomposition of $x_s$ on each $V_i\otimes_{{\mathds Z}_\ell} \overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$ is defined over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.
It follows that $x_s$ belongs to $\mathcal G(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$.
Since $r(I_K)$ is finite, there is an integer $m>0$ such that $x^m_s$ commutes with $r(I_K)$.
Let $D$ be the schematic closure of $\langle x_s^m\rangle$ in ${\mathcal G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$.
Then $D$ is diagonalizable and commutes with $r(W_K)$.
The relation $\operatorname{Ad}(x_s^m)(N)=q^{-m}N$ shows that $D$ acts on $N$ via a character $\psi\colon D\to\mathbb{G}_{m,\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$.
Since $\psi(x_s^m)=q^{-m}$, the order of $\psi$ is infinite.
We claim that $\psi\colon D(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)\to \overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell^\times$ is surjective.
Indeed, under the identification $D(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)=\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}\nolimits(X^*(D),\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell^\times)$, this map is the restriction
\[
\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}\nolimits(X^*(D),\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell^\times)
\longrightarrow
\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}\nolimits({\mathds Z}\psi,\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell^\times)\simeq \overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell^\times.
\]
Since $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell^\times$ is divisible, every homomorphism on ${\mathds Z}\psi\subset X^*(D)$ extends to $X^*(D)$.
An element $h\in D(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$ with $\psi(h)=a$ therefore conjugates $(r,N)$ to $(r,aN)$.

label: Lemma: smoothness of Frobenius centralizer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Lemma: smoothness of Frobenius centralizer}
Keep the notation of
\Cref{Example: integral Weil-Deligne construction}.
Let $\rho=(r,N)$ be a $\mathcal{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representation of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ whose generic fiber is Frobenius semisimple.
Assume that there exists a geometric Frobenius lift $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q\in W_K$ such that, for every $i$, any two distinct eigenvalues $a, b$ of $r(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q)$ on $V_i\otimes_{{\mathds Z}_\ell}\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$ satisfy $a-b\in\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell^\times$.
Then the scheme-theoretic centralizer $ Z_{\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}}(r(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q)) $ is smooth over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.
Moreover, $ Z_{\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}}(r(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q)) $ contains a maximal torus of $\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $x\coloneqq r(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q)$.
As in the proof of \Cref{Proposition: independence of integral WD construction}, the assumptions imply that the eigenspace decomposition of $x$ on each $V_i\otimes_{{\mathds Z}_\ell} \overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$ is defined over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.
Let $D$ be the schematic closure of $\langle x\rangle$ in $\mathcal G_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$.
Then $D$ is diagonalizable and
\[
Z_{\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}}(x)
=Z_{\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}}(D).
\]
Since $Z_{\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}}(D)$ is smooth by \cite[Lemma~2.2.4]{Conrad2014}, the first assertion follows.
The second assertion follows from \cite[Remark~3.1.5 and Theorem~3.2.6]{Conrad2014}.

head: environment

label: Lemma:weight cocharacter is associated with the monodromy operator
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Lemma:weight cocharacter is associated with the monodromy operator}
    Let $\rho=(r,N)$ be a $\mathbf{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representation of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}$ and assume that $\rho$ is pure.
    Let $w \colon \mathbb{G}_m \to \mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}$ be the Frobenius-weight cocharacter of $r$ and put $\lambda\coloneqq w^{-1}$.
    Then $\lambda$ is associated to $N$ in the sense of \textup{\cite[5.3, Definition]{Jantzen}}.
head: environment
labels: Lemma:weight cocharacter is associated with the monodromy operator

title: Proof
body_md:
We choose a faithful representation $V$ of $\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell}$.
By \cite[5.12, Claim]{Jantzen}, it suffices to show that $\lambda$ is associated to $N$ in $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(V)$.
We write $V=\bigoplus_{j \in {\mathds Z}} V(\lambda, j)$ for the weight decomposition with respect to $\lambda$.
We have $N(V(\lambda, j))\subset V(\lambda, j+2)$ and $N^j\colon V(\lambda, -j) 
  \mathrel{\overset{\raisebox{-0.35ex}{$\scriptstyle\sim$}}{\rightarrow}} 
 V(\lambda, j)$ for $j\geq0$ by purity.
By the Jacobson--Morozov theorem, these isomorphisms give an $\mathop{\mathfrak{sl}}\nolimits_2$-triple $(N,d\lambda(1),F)$ in $\mathop{\mathrm{End}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell}(V)$.
Hence $\lambda$ is associated to $N$ in $\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(V)$ by \cite[5.5, Proposition]{Jantzen}.
See also \cite[Proposition~(1.6.9)]{WeilII}.

label: Proposition:uniqueness of monodromy operator rational case
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Proposition:uniqueness of monodromy operator rational case}
Let $\rho_i=(r_i,N_i)$, for $i=1,2$, be Frobenius semisimple $\mathbf{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representations of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}$ which are pure with respect to $\mu$.
If $r_1$ and $r_2$ are $\mathbf{G}(\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell})$-conjugate, then
\[
    \rho_1 \sim_{\mathbf{G}(\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell})} \rho_2.
\]
head: environment
labels: Proposition:uniqueness of monodromy operator rational case

title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume that $r \coloneqq r_1=r_2$, and we let $w$ be the Frobenius-weight cocharacter determined by $r$.
    Let $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits\coloneqq \mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits(\mathbf{G})_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}$ and let $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits = \bigoplus_\tau \mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau$ be the isotypic decomposition of $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits$ as a $W_K$-representation, where $\tau$ runs over the isomorphism classes of irreducible $W_K$-representations over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}$ and $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau$ denotes the $\tau$-isotypic component.
    Put $\lambda \coloneqq w^{-1}$.
    Since $r$ commutes with $\lambda$, each component $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau$ is stable under the action of $\lambda$.
    Hence we have the weight decomposition
\[
\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau=\bigoplus_{n\in {\mathds Z}}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau(\lambda,n),
\]
where $\lambda(z)$ acts on $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau(\lambda,n)$ as $z^n$.

Let $P \coloneqq P_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(\lambda)$ be the parabolic subgroup associated with $\lambda$.
We note that $\mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits(P)= \bigoplus_{\tau,n\geq0}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau(\lambda,n)$.
By \Cref{Lemma:weight cocharacter is associated with the monodromy operator}, the cocharacter $\lambda$ is associated to both $N_1$ and $N_2$.
By \cite[5.9, Proposition]{Jantzen} (see also \cite[Lemma~5.7]{Cotner}), the map $\bigoplus_{\tau, n \geq 0}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau(\lambda,n) \to \bigoplus_{\tau, n \geq 2}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau(\lambda,n)$ defined by $Y \mapsto [Y, N_1]$ is surjective.
Since each component $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_\tau(\lambda,n)$ is mapped to $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{q^{\alpha} \cdot \tau}(\lambda,n+2)$, where $q^{\alpha} \cdot \tau$ is the $W_K$-representation defined by $g \mapsto q^{\alpha(g)} \cdot \tau(g)$, we see that the induced map $\bigoplus_{n \geq 0}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_1(\lambda,n) \to \bigoplus_{n \geq 2}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{q^{\alpha}}(\lambda,n)$ is surjective, where $1$ denotes the trivial $W_K$-representation.

Let $Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(r)$ be the scheme-theoretic centralizer of $r(W_K)$.
In our setting, we have
\[
Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(r)\subset Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(\lambda)\subset P,
\]
and thus the equalities $Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(r)\cap P=Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(r)$ and $\bigoplus_{n \geq 0}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_1(\lambda,n) = \mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits (Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(r))$ hold.
We also note that $Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(r)$ is smooth since the characteristic is zero.
It follows that the orbit map $Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(r) \to \bigoplus_{n \geq 2}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{q^{\alpha}}(\lambda,n)$ defined by $g \mapsto \operatorname{Ad}(g)(N_1)$ has a dense open image.
Similarly, the orbit map $Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(r) \to \bigoplus_{n \geq 2}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{q^{\alpha}}(\lambda,n)$ defined by $g \mapsto \operatorname{Ad}(g)(N_2)$ also has a dense open image.
Since these two images are dense open subsets of the irreducible affine space $\bigoplus_{n \geq 2}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{q^\alpha}(\lambda,n)$, they intersect.
In particular, $N_1$ and $N_2$ are conjugate by an element of $Z_{\mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell}}}(r)(\overline{{\mathds Q}}_{\ell})$, as desired.

label: Definition:integral G-valued purity
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{Definition:integral G-valued purity}
Let $\rho=(r, N)$ be a $\mathcal{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representation of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.
We say that $\rho$ is \textit{pure} (with respect to $\mu$) if the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The generic fiber $\rho_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell}$ is pure with respect to $\mu$.
\item The Frobenius-weight cocharacter $w \colon \mathbb{G}_m \to \mathbf{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell}$ of $r$ extends over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.
\item The scheme-theoretic centralizer $H\coloneqq  Z_{\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}}(r)$ of $r(W_K)$ is smooth over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.
\item Put $\lambda\coloneqq w^{-1}$ and
\[
\mathcal V\coloneqq 
\{
X\in\bigoplus_{n\geq2}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}(\lambda,n) \mid
\operatorname{Ad}(r(\sigma))(X)=q^{\alpha(\sigma)}X
\text{ for every }\sigma\in W_K
 \},
\]
where $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}=\bigoplus_{n \in {\mathds Z}}\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}(\lambda,n)$ is the weight decomposition with respect to $\lambda$.
Then the map $ \mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits(H)\to \mathcal V $ defined by $Y\mapsto[Y,N]$ is surjective.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: Proposition:uniqueness of monodromy operator integral case
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Proposition:uniqueness of monodromy operator integral case}
Let $\rho_i=(r_i,N_i)$ for $i=1,2$ be $\mathcal{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representations of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ which are pure with respect to $\mu$ (in the sense of \Cref{Definition:integral G-valued purity}) and whose generic fibers are Frobenius semisimple.
If $r_1$ and $r_2$ are $\mathcal{G}(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_{\ell})$-conjugate, then
\[
    \rho_1 \sim_{\mathcal{G}(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_{\ell})} \rho_2.
\]
head: environment
labels: Proposition:uniqueness of monodromy operator integral case

title: Proof
body_md:
Our argument is inspired by the proof of
\cite[Theorem~5.11]{Cotner}.
We may assume that $r\coloneqq r_1=r_2$.
Let $w \colon \mathbb{G}_m \to \mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$ be the Frobenius-weight cocharacter of $r$ and put $\lambda\coloneqq w^{-1}$.
Let $H$ and $\mathcal V$ be as in \Cref{Definition:integral G-valued purity}.
The adjoint action of $H$ preserves $\mathcal V$ and $N_1,N_2\in\mathcal V$.
We also write $\mathcal V$ for the corresponding affine space.
For $i=1,2$, consider the orbit map $ f_i\colon H \to \mathcal V, $ $h\mapsto\operatorname{Ad}(h)(N_i)$.
Its differential at the identity is surjective by the assumption.
Since $H$ and $\mathcal V$ are smooth, this implies that $f_i$ is smooth.
In particular, the reduction $(f_i)_{\overline{{\mathds F}}_\ell}$ has a dense open image for $i=1, 2$.
These two images intersect, and there is an element $\overline h\in H(\overline{{\mathds F}}_\ell)$ such that $\operatorname{Ad}(\overline h)(N_1 \otimes_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell} \overline{{\mathds F}}_\ell)=N_2 \otimes_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell} \overline{{\mathds F}}_\ell$.
The fiber $f_1^{-1}(N_2)$ is smooth over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ and has the $\overline{{\mathds F}}_\ell$-point $\overline h$.
Since $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ is henselian, this point lifts to an element $h\in H(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$ satisfying $\operatorname{Ad}(h)(N_1)=N_2$.
As $h$ centralizes $r$, it conjugates $\rho_1$ to $\rho_2$.

label: Lemma: sufficient criterion for integral purity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Lemma: sufficient criterion for integral purity}
Let $\rho=(r,N)$ be a $\mathcal{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representation of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ whose generic fiber is Frobenius semisimple.
Assume that $\rho$ satisfies conditions (1)--(3) of \Cref{Definition:integral G-valued purity}.
Let $ \mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell} =\bigoplus_\tau\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell,\tau} $ be the isotypic decomposition for the $W_K$-action, and put $ \mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell,\tau} \coloneqq \mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell} \cap\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell,\tau}. $ Assume that
\[
\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}
=\bigoplus_\tau\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell,\tau}
\]
and that the cokernel of
\[
d \colon
\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}\longrightarrow
\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}, \quad Y \mapsto [Y,N]
\]
is torsion-free.
Then $\rho$ is pure with respect to $\mu$.
head: environment
labels: Lemma: sufficient criterion for integral purity

title: Proof
body_md:
It remains to verify condition (4).
Let $\lambda\coloneqq w^{-1}$ and let $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell,\tau}= \bigoplus_{n \in {\mathds Z}} \mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell,\tau}(\lambda, n)$ be the weight decomposition with respect to $\lambda$.
As in the proof of \Cref{Proposition:uniqueness of monodromy operator rational case},
\[
d \colon \bigoplus_{n\geq0}
\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell,1}(\lambda,n)
\longrightarrow
\bigoplus_{n\geq2}
\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell,q^\alpha}(\lambda,n)
\]
is surjective after tensoring with $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$.
Its cokernel is a torsion-free $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$-module by the assumptions, and hence it is zero.
As $\lambda$ is central in $H$, the source is $\mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits(H)$, and the target is $\mathcal V$.
This shows that $\rho$ satisfies condition (4).

label: prop:global Frobenius semisimplicity
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since Frobenius semisimplicity is invariant under finite extensions of $K$, we may assume that $K=K^c$.
We first show that $\rho_{\ell, 2}$ is Frobenius semisimple for every $\ell$.

If $b_2(X)\geq 4$, the Kuga--Satake construction \cite{Andre96b} (see also \cite[Lemma~4.6]{ArithmeticNagai} and \Cref{subsection:Strong compatibility of Mumford--Tate-valued Weil representations}) reduces the assertion to the corresponding result for abelian varieties, which follows from \cite[Expos\'e~IX]{SGA7-I} when $\ell\neq p$ and from \cite{Coleman-Iovita} when $\ell=p$.

If $b_2(X)=3$, then $H^{1,1}(X_{\mathds C})$ is spanned by a polarization whose orthogonal complement in $H^2_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q})$ has rank two.
The corresponding special orthogonal group is a torus, which in turn implies that $\mathbf{G}_2$ is a torus.
This implies the assertion.

Now write $\rho^{\operatorname{MT}}_\ell=(r^{\operatorname{MT}}_\ell,N^{\operatorname{MT}}_\ell)$, and let $x$ be the value of $r^{\operatorname{MT}}_\ell$ at a geometric Frobenius lift.
Write $x=x_sx_u$ for its Jordan decomposition.
Since $p_2(x)$ is semisimple, we have $p_2(x_u)=1$.
The kernel of $p_2$ contains no nontrivial unipotent elements, so $x_u=1$.
Therefore $\rho^{\operatorname{MT}}_\ell$ is Frobenius semisimple.
This implies that $\rho_{\ell, i}$ is also Frobenius semisimple for every $i$.

label: lem:weighted tensor generation
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) The kernel of $p_2$ is generated by $s$, which acts on $V_i$ as $(-1)^i$ and hence trivially on $V^{\otimes 2}_i$.
The assertion follows since $p_2$ is surjective.

(2) The group $\mathbf{G}_2$ is reductive, and $V_2$ is faithful as a $\mathbf{G}_2$-representation.
Thus $V^{\otimes 2}_i$ is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of $ V_2^{\otimes m}\otimes  V_2^{\vee,\otimes n} $ for some $m,n\geq 0$ by \cite[Theorems~4.14 and~22.42]{Milne17}.
The scalar subgroup $\mathbb{G}_m\subset\mathbf{G}_2$ acts on
$V_i^{\otimes2}$ as $z^i$ and on
$V_2^{\otimes m}\otimes V_2^{\vee,\otimes n}$
as $z^{m-n}$.
Thus we may assume that $m-n=i$, as required.
head: environment

label: lem:tensor-square defector of purity
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $V$ be the underlying vector space of $\rho$ and let $M_\bullet V$ be the monodromy filtration of $N$.
The monodromy operator on $V\otimes V$ is $N\otimes 1+1\otimes N$.
Its monodromy filtration is the convolution of the two filtrations, so
\[
 \text{\rm gr}_m^M(V\otimes V)\simeq\bigoplus_{a+b=m}\text{\rm gr}_a^M V\otimes\text{\rm gr}_b^M V.
\]
This follows, for instance, from the Jacobson--Morozov theorem; see \cite[Proposition~(1.6.9)]{WeilII}.

Let $a$ be an eigenvalue of geometric Frobenius on $\text{\rm gr}_j^M V$.
Then $a^2$ is an eigenvalue on the summand $\text{\rm gr}_j^M V\otimes\text{\rm gr}_j^M V$ of $\text{\rm gr}_{2j}^M(V\otimes V)$.
Purity of $V\otimes V$ says that $a^2$ is a Weil $q^{2(i+j)}$-number.
It follows that $a$ is a Weil $q^{i+j}$-number, as desired.

label: Theorem:purity of Weil-Deligne representations
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since purity is invariant under finite extensions, we may assume that $K=K^c$.
Using \Cref{lem:weighted tensor generation} and the \'etale--Betti comparison, we see that $H^i_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline{K}}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)^{\otimes 2}$ is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of $ H^2_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline{K}}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)^{\otimes m}\otimes H^2_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline{K}}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)^{\vee,\otimes n} $ with $m-n=i$ as a $\mathbf{G}_2$-representation over ${\mathds Q}_\ell$.
Since the action of $G_K$ on total cohomology factors through $\phi^{\operatorname{MT}}_\ell\colon G_K\to\mathbf{G}({\mathds Q}_\ell)$, it follows that this splitting is also $G_K$-equivariant.
Thus $\rho_{\ell,i}^{\otimes 2}$ is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of Weil--Deligne representations $ \rho_{\ell,2}^{\otimes m}\otimes \rho_{\ell,2}^{\vee,\otimes n} $ with $m-n=i$.
By \Cref{lem:WMC in degree 2}, $\rho_{\ell,2}$ is pure of weight $2$, so each $ \rho_{\ell,2}^{\otimes m}\otimes \rho_{\ell,2}^{\vee,\otimes n} $ is pure of weight $2(m-n)=2i$.
Hence $\rho_{\ell,i}^{\otimes 2}$ is pure of weight $2i$.
The assertion now follows from \Cref{lem:tensor-square defector of purity}.

label: Remark:difference Kisin-Zhou
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{Remark:difference Kisin-Zhou}
Extension of scalars from $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$ to ${\mathds C}$ induces a bijection between the $G_{\mathds Q}$-invariant equivalence classes of $\mathbf{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representations of $F_v$ over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$ and the $\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}\nolimits({\mathds C}/{\mathds Q})$-invariant equivalence classes of $\mathbf{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representations of $F_v$ over ${\mathds C}$.
The latter are called ``defined over ${\mathds Q}$'' in \cite[Definition~4.1.7]{KZb}.
Indeed, after fixing a finite quotient through which the inertia subgroup acts, $\mathbf{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representations are parametrized by an affine scheme of finite type over ${\mathds Q}$.
An $\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}\nolimits({\mathds C}/{\mathds Q})$-invariant $\mathbf{G}$-conjugacy orbit is locally closed and descends to $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$, so it has a $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$-point.
Moreover, two $\mathbf{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representations over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$ that are equivalent over ${\mathds C}$ are already equivalent over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$ since their transporter is a scheme of finite type over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$, and hence has a $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$-point whenever it has a ${\mathds C}$-point.
This proves the desired bijection.

Thus \Cref{Definition:rational strong compatibility} is equivalent to the formulation of strong compatibility used in \cite{KZb}.

label: Definition: Kuga-Satake abelian variety
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{Definition: Kuga-Satake abelian variety}
Let $E \subset \overline{F}$ be a finite extension of $F$.
We say that $X$ \textit{admits a Kuga--Satake abelian variety over $E$ of dimension $2^{b_2(X)-1}$} if there exists an abelian variety $A$ over $E$ with an isomorphism of ${\mathds Q}$-vector spaces
\[
\theta \colon H^1_B(A_{\mathds C}, {\mathds Q}) \stackrel{\textstyle\sim}{\smash{\longrightarrow}\rule{0pt}{0.4ex}}\mathop{\mathrm{Cl}}\nolimits(V^2_{B}(1))
\]
satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let
\[
\mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits
\hookrightarrow \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^1_B(A_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q}))
\]
be the injection obtained via $\theta$ from left multiplication on $\mathop{\mathrm{Cl}}\nolimits(V^2_{B}(1))$.
The Hodge cocharacter $\mu_{A} \colon \mathbb{G}_{m, {\mathds C}} \to \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^1_B(A_{{\mathds C}}, {\mathds C}))$ factors through $\mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits_{\mathds C}$, and the composition $\mathbb{G}_{m, {\mathds C}} \xrightarrow{\mu_{A}} \mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits_{\mathds C} \xrightarrow{\pi} \mathop{\mathrm{SO}}\nolimits_{\mathds C}$ is equal to the Hodge cocharacter associated with $V^2_B(1)$.

\item For every prime $\ell$, the Galois representation
\[
\phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{KS}}\nolimits}_{\ell} \colon G_E \longrightarrow \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^1_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(A_{\overline{F}}, {\mathds Q}_\ell))
\]
factors through $\mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits({\mathds Q}_\ell)$ (via the \'etale--Betti comparison), and via $\pi \colon \mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits_{{\mathds Q}_\ell} \to \mathop{\mathrm{SO}}\nolimits_{{\mathds Q}_\ell}$, this induces the usual $G_E$-action on $V^2_\ell(1)\coloneqq H^2_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline{F}}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)(1)$.
Moreover, the composition $G_E 
\xrightarrow{\phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{KS}}\nolimits}_{\ell}} \mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits({\mathds Q}_\ell) \xrightarrow{\nu} {\mathds Q}^\times_\ell$ is the inverse of the cyclotomic character $\chi_\ell$.
\end{enumerate}
We call such an abelian variety $A$, equipped with $\theta$, a \emph{Kuga--Satake abelian variety of $X$ over $E$}.
head: environment

label: Lemma: existence of KS abelian variety
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Lemma: existence of KS abelian variety}
Let $\mathscr{L}$ be an ample line bundle on $X$ and put
\[
\Lambda_{\widehat{\mathds Z}}
\coloneqq H^2_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline F},\widehat{\mathds Z}(1)),
\quad
P_{\widehat{\mathds Z}}
\coloneqq c_1(\mathscr{L})^\perp\subset\Lambda_{\widehat{\mathds Z}},
\]
where the orthogonal complement is taken with respect to the BBF form.
Write $P_{{\mathds A}_f} \coloneqq P_{\widehat{\mathds Z}}\otimes_{\widehat{\mathds Z}}{\mathds A}_f$ for finite adèles ${\mathds A}_f$ of ${\mathds Q}$.
For $m=3$ or $m=4$, let $\mathop{\mathrm{K}}\nolimits_m^{\operatorname{ad}}$ be the image of
\[
\mathop{\mathrm{K}}\nolimits_m\coloneqq 
\Set*{
g\in
\mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits(P_{{\mathds A}_f})\cap\mathop{\mathrm{Cl}}\nolimits(P_{\widehat{\mathds Z}})^\times
\;\delimsize\vert\; g-1\in m\mathop{\mathrm{Cl}}\nolimits(P_{\widehat{\mathds Z}})
}
\]
under the natural projection to $\mathop{\mathrm{SO}}\nolimits(P_{\widehat{\mathds Z}})$.
Let $E/F$ be a finite extension such that the image of $G_E \to \mathrm{O}(P_{\widehat{\mathds Z}})$ is contained in $\mathop{\mathrm{K}}\nolimits_m^{\operatorname{ad}}$.
Then $X$ admits a Kuga--Satake abelian variety $A$ over $E$ in the sense of \Cref{Definition: Kuga-Satake abelian variety}.
Moreover, $A$ can be chosen to have semistable reduction at every finite place of $E$ of residue characteristic prime to $m$.
head: environment
labels: Lemma: existence of KS abelian variety

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite[Theorem~8.4.3]{Andre96b}, the assumption ensures that the Kuga--Satake construction associated with the even Clifford algebra of the primitive cohomology can be carried out over $E$, yielding a Kuga--Satake package in the sense of \cite[Definition~4.5.1]{Andre96b} such that all $m$-torsion points of the underlying abelian variety $B/E$ are rational over $E$.
(Strictly speaking, we use a different quadratic form from the one in \cite{Andre96b}, but the same argument applies.)
We set $A\coloneqq B^4$.
Using \cite[Variant~4.1.3 and Corollary~6.4.4]{Andre96b}, together with \cite[Lemma~4.6]{ArithmeticNagai}, one can check that there is an isomorphism $\theta \colon H^1_B(A_{\mathds C}, {\mathds Q})  
  \mathrel{\overset{\raisebox{-0.35ex}{$\scriptstyle\sim$}}{\rightarrow}} 
 \mathop{\mathrm{Cl}}\nolimits(V^2_{B}(1))$ such that $A$, equipped with $\theta$, is a Kuga--Satake abelian variety over $E$ in the sense of \Cref{Definition: Kuga-Satake abelian variety}.

Since all $m$-torsion points of $A$ are $E$-rational, it follows from Raynaud's criterion \cite[Expos\'e~IX, Proposition~4.7]{SGA7-I} that $A$ has semistable reduction at every finite place of $E$ of residue characteristic prime to $m$.

label: Lemma: LLV and Kuga-Satake hodge structure
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Lemma: LLV and Kuga-Satake hodge structure}
The composition $\mathbb{G}_{m,{\mathds C}}\xrightarrow{\mu_A}\mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits_{\mathds C}\xrightarrow{R}\prod_i\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^i_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds C}))$ is the Hodge cocharacter $\mu_X$ of $H^\bullet_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q})$.
In particular, we have the following commutative diagram:
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\operatorname{MT}(A_{{\mathds C}}) \arrow[r] \arrow[d, hook]
&
\mathbf{G} \arrow[d, hook]
\\
\mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits \arrow[r, "R"]
&
R(\mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits) \arrow[r, hook]
&
\displaystyle \prod_i \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^i_B(X_{{\mathds C}},{\mathds Q})).
\end{tikzcd}
\]
The upper horizontal map is the restriction of $R$ and is an isogeny.
head: environment
labels: Lemma: LLV and Kuga-Satake hodge structure

title: Proof
body_md:
Both $\mu_X$ and $R\circ\mu_A$ take values in $R(\mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits)_{\mathds C}$.
Since the projection
\[
p_2 \colon \prod_i \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^i_B(X_{{\mathds C}}, {\mathds Q})) \longrightarrow \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^2_B(X_{{\mathds C}}, {\mathds Q}))
\]
    induces a central isogeny from $R(\mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits)$ onto its image, it is enough to show that their degree-two projections are the same.
    Since $p_2\circ R=\nu\cdot\pi$, the required equality follows immediately.
    By the defining property of Mumford--Tate groups, the equality $R\circ\mu_A=\mu_X$ implies $R(\operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C}))=\mathbf{G}$.
    Since $\nu\cdot\pi$ has finite kernel, so does $R$.
    Thus the restriction $R\colon\operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C})\to\mathbf{G}$ is an isogeny.

label: Proposition:LLV and Kuga-Satake
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Proposition:LLV and Kuga-Satake}
Keep the notation and assumptions above.
Let $s \in Z(\mathbf{G})({\mathds Q})$ be the element which acts as $(-1)^i$ on $H^i_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q})$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For every $\ell$, the homomorphism $\phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{KS}}\nolimits}_\ell \colon G_E \to \mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits({\mathds Q}_\ell)$ factors through $\operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C})({\mathds Q}_\ell)$.
    \item There is a unique continuous character $\epsilon \colon G_E \to \langle s \rangle =\{ 1, s \}$ such that the following diagram commutes for every $\ell$:
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
G_E
\arrow[r, "\phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{KS}}\nolimits}_{\ell}"]
\arrow[dr, "\epsilon\phi^{\operatorname{MT}}_{\ell}"']
&
\operatorname{MT}(A_{{\mathds C}})({\mathds Q}_\ell)
\arrow[d, "R"]
\\
&
\mathbf{G}({\mathds Q}_\ell).
\end{tikzcd}
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) We choose an ample line bundle on $X$, and write $\eta$ for its class in $V^2_B(1)$.
    Let $H \subset \mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits$ be the stabilizer of $\eta$ with respect to its usual action on $V^2_B(1)$ via $\pi$.
    By the properties of the Kuga--Satake abelian variety, we have $\operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C})\subset H$ and $\phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{KS}}\nolimits}_\ell(G_E)\subset H({\mathds Q}_\ell).$ We define $f \colon H\to\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^2_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q}))$ by $f=(p_2\circ R)|_H =(\nu\cdot\pi)|_H$.
    Then the kernel of $f$ is $\{ \pm 1 \} \subset H$.
    Let $\operatorname{MT}_2(X_{\mathds C}) \subset \mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^2_B(X_{\mathds C}, {\mathds Q}))$ be the Mumford--Tate group of degree $2$.
    Since $\operatorname{MT}(A_{{\mathds C}})$ contains $\{ \pm 1 \}$ and $f(\operatorname{MT}(A_{{\mathds C}}))=\operatorname{MT}_2(X_{\mathds C})$, it follows that $f^{-1}(\operatorname{MT}_2(X_{\mathds C})) = \operatorname{MT}(A_{{\mathds C}})$.
    By our assumption, the Galois representation $\phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{KS}}\nolimits}_\ell$ takes values in $f^{-1}(\operatorname{MT}_2(X_{\mathds C}))$, which proves (1).

(2) For each $\ell$, we define $ \epsilon_\ell \colon G_E \to \langle s \rangle $ by $\epsilon_\ell(\sigma)=\phi^{\operatorname{MT}}_\ell(\sigma) \cdot (R\circ \phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{KS}}\nolimits}_\ell)(\sigma)^{-1}$.
We have to show that $\epsilon_\ell$ is independent of $\ell$.
For this, it suffices to show that the subgroup $\ker(\epsilon_\ell) \subset G_E$ is independent of $\ell$.

Let $J_\ell \subset \operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C})_{{\mathds Q}_\ell} \times\mathbf{G}_{{\mathds Q}_\ell}$ be the Zariski closure of the image of
\[
  \tau_\ell\coloneqq 
  (\phi_\ell^{\mathop{\mathrm{KS}}\nolimits}, \phi_\ell^{\operatorname{MT}})
  \colon G_E \longrightarrow
  \operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C})({\mathds Q}_\ell)\times\mathbf{G}({\mathds Q}_\ell).
\]
We claim that $\tau^{-1}_\ell(J^\circ_\ell({\mathds Q}_\ell)) = \ker(\epsilon_\ell)$.
This implies that $\ker(\epsilon_\ell)$ is independent of $\ell$ by a theorem of Serre \cite{RibetLetter} (see also \cite[Proposition~(6.14)]{LarsenPink92}).
To show the claim, let $\Gamma_R\subset\operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C})\times\mathbf{G}$ be the graph of $R$.
Since $\mathbf{G} \to \operatorname{MT}_2(X_{\mathds C})$ is an isogeny, the degree-two comparison shows that $ J_\ell^\circ\subset(\Gamma_R)_{{\mathds Q}_\ell}; $ see also the proof of \cite[Proposition~4.7]{ArithmeticNagai}.
Since $R\colon\operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C})\to\mathbf{G}$ is an isogeny, \Cref{thm: MT conjecture} implies that $J_\ell^\circ$ and $(\Gamma_R)_{{\mathds Q}_\ell}$ have the same dimension.
Hence $J_\ell^\circ=(\Gamma_R)_{{\mathds Q}_\ell}$.
Consequently, we have $\tau^{-1}_\ell(J^\circ_\ell({\mathds Q}_\ell)) = \ker(\epsilon_\ell)$.
This completes the proof of (2).

label: Theorem: strong compatibility of MT representation
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Theorem: strong compatibility of MT representation}
Let $X$ be a hyper-Kähler~ variety over a number field $F$ with $b_2(X)\geq4$.
Assume that the algebraic monodromy group of $H^\bullet_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline F},{\mathds Q}_\ell)$ is connected for every $\ell$, and that $X$ admits a Kuga--Satake abelian variety $A$ over $F$ with semistable reduction at a finite place $v\mid p$ of $F$.
Let $\mathbf{G}\coloneqq \operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})$ and consider the associated $\mathbf{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representation $\rho^{\operatorname{MT}}_{\ell,v}$ of $F_v$ over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$.
Then $\{\rho^{\operatorname{MT}}_{\ell,v}\}_\ell$ is rationally strongly compatible in the sense of \Cref{Definition:rational strong compatibility}.
head: environment
labels: Theorem: strong compatibility of MT representation

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{Lemma: LLV and Kuga-Satake hodge structure} and \Cref{Proposition:LLV and Kuga-Satake}, there are an isogeny $R\colon \operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C}) \to\mathbf{G}$ over ${\mathds Q}$ and a continuous character $\epsilon\colon G_F\to\langle s\rangle$ such that $ R\circ\phi^{\mathop{\mathrm{KS}}\nolimits}_\ell=\epsilon\phi^{\operatorname{MT}}_\ell $ for every $\ell$.
By \Cref{Theorem:strongly compatiblity for abelian variety}, there exists an $\operatorname{MT}(A_{\mathds C})$-valued Weil--Deligne representation $\rho^A_v=(r^A_v,N^A_v)$ of $F_v$ over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$ realizing the resulting rationally strongly compatible system.
Write $\epsilon_v$ for the restriction of $\epsilon$ to $W_{F_v}$ and set
\[
\rho_v\coloneqq (\epsilon_v\cdot(R\circ r^A_v),\,dR(N^A_v) ).
\]
Since $R$ is defined over ${\mathds Q}$ and $\epsilon_v$ takes values in $Z(\mathbf{G})({\mathds Q})$, the $\mathbf{G}(\overline{{\mathds Q}})$-conjugacy class of $\rho_v$ is $G_{\mathds Q}$-invariant.
The constructions given in \Cref{Example: WD rep ell adic case,Example: WD rep p adic case} are compatible with tensor products and send the finite-order character $\epsilon|_{G_{F_v}}$ to $(\epsilon_v,0)$.
Together with functoriality under $R$, we see that
\[
(\rho_v)_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell}
\sim_{\mathbf{G}(\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell)}
\rho^{\operatorname{MT}}_{\ell,v}
\]
for every $\ell$, including $\ell=p$.
This proves the assertion.
head: environment

label: Remark: local strong compatibility
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{Remark: local strong compatibility}
The assertion of \Cref{Theorem: strong compatibility of MT representation} also holds over a finite extension $K/{\mathds Q}_p$ equipped with an embedding $K\hookrightarrow{\mathds C}$.
More precisely, let $X$ be a hyper-Kähler~ variety over $K$ with $b_2(X)\geq4$.
Assume that, for every $\ell$, the Galois representation on $H^\bullet_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline K},{\mathds Q}_\ell)$ takes values in $\operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})({\mathds Q}_\ell)$, and that $X$ admits a Kuga--Satake abelian variety over $K$ with semistable reduction.
Then the associated $\operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})$-valued Weil--Deligne representations form a rationally strongly compatible system.
(Here the notions of a Kuga--Satake abelian variety and rational strong compatibility are understood by extending the definitions above to this local setting in the obvious way.)
Indeed, the comparison with Kuga--Satake abelian varieties also holds in this setting by descent to a finitely generated subfield of $K$ and then the same proof applies using the local version of \Cref{Theorem:strongly compatiblity for abelian variety}; see \cite[Remark~5.3.13]{KZb}.
head: environment

label: Corollary: independence of Frobenius eigenvalues
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{Corollary: independence of Frobenius eigenvalues}
Let $K$ be a finite extension of ${\mathds Q}_p$, and let $X$ be a hyper-Kähler~ variety over $K$.
For every $\ell$ and $i$, let $\rho_{\ell,i}=(r_{\ell,i},N_{\ell,i})$ be the Weil--Deligne representation of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell$ associated with $H^i_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline K},{\mathds Q}_\ell)$.
There exists a finite extension $L/K$ such that, for every $i$ and every geometric Frobenius lift $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_L\in W_L$, the characteristic polynomial $ \det (T-r_{\ell,i}(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_L)) $ belongs to ${\mathds Z}[T]$ and is independent of $\ell$, including $\ell=p$.
If $b_2(X)=3$, one may take $L=K$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix an embedding $\overline{K}\hookrightarrow{\mathds C}$.
Suppose first that $b_2(X)=3$.
Then $\operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})$ is a torus.
Thus, by \Cref{thm: MT conjecture}, we see that $H^i_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline K},{\mathds Q}_\ell)$ is potentially unramified if $\ell \neq p$ and potentially crystalline if $\ell = p$ for all $i$.
By the weight--monodromy theorem (\Cref{Theorem:purity of Weil-Deligne representations}), all the Frobenius eigenvalues in degree $i$ are therefore of weight $i$.
By \cite[Theorems~B and~D]{Ochiai}, the alternating traces of all positive powers of $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_K$ are rational and independent of $\ell$, including $\ell=p$.
Thus the alternating product of characteristic polynomials is rational and independent of $\ell$.
Since different cohomological degrees have distinct weights, each factor has the same properties as well.

Suppose now that $b_2(X)\geq4$.
After a finite extension $L/K$, the Galois representations are valued in the Mumford--Tate group, and $X_L$ admits a Kuga--Satake abelian variety over $L$ with semistable reduction.
The assertion then follows from \Cref{Remark: local strong compatibility}.

Finally, the Frobenius eigenvalues for $\ell\neq p$ are algebraic integers by \cite[Proposition~2.1]{Ochiai}.
Hence the common characteristic polynomials belong to ${\mathds Z}[T]$ for all $\ell$ (including $\ell =p$).

label: ex:nontrivial central inertia character
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:nontrivial central inertia character}
Let $F$ be a number field, let $v\mid 3$, and let $C$ be an elliptic curve over $F$ such that $ \mathop{\mathrm{End}}\nolimits_F(C)_{\mathds Q}=\mathop{\mathrm{End}}\nolimits_{\overline F}(C_{\overline F})_{\mathds Q}\simeq{\mathds Q}(\sqrt{-1})$ and all $3$-torsion points of $C$ are rational over $F$.
Suppose that there is a quadratic character $\epsilon \colon G_F\to\{\pm1\}$, ramified at $v$, such that the quadratic twist $C^\epsilon$ of $C$ by $\epsilon$ has good reduction at $v$.
Then for every $\ell \neq 3$, the inertia subgroup $I_v$ acts on $H^1_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(C_{\overline F}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)$ through the character $\epsilon$.

Let $S\coloneqq  C \times C$ and let $X=K_2(S)$ be the associated generalized Kummer fourfold over $F$.
We have $G_F$-equivariant decompositions
\[
\begin{aligned}
H^2_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline F}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)&\simeq H^2_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(S_{\overline F}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)\oplus{\mathds Q}_\ell(-1),\\
H^3_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline F}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)&\simeq H^3_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(S_{\overline F}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)\oplus H^1_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(S_{\overline F}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)(-1),\\
H^4_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline F}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)&\simeq\mathop{\mathrm{Sym}}\nolimits^2 H^2_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline F}, {\mathds Q}_\ell)\oplus {\mathds Q}_\ell(-2)^{ \oplus 80}
\end{aligned}
\]
and similarly for Betti cohomology groups.
For the third identification, see \cite[Theorem~1.1]{FH23}.
These decompositions are obtained from algebraic correspondences defined over $F$ and are compatible with the \'etale--Betti comparison.

Put
\[
T\coloneqq \operatorname{MT}(C_{\mathds C})\simeq
\operatorname{Res}_{{\mathds Q}(\sqrt{-1})/{\mathds Q}}\mathbb{G}_m.
\]
Since all endomorphisms of $C_{\overline{F}}$ are defined over $F$, the Galois representation on $H^1_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(C_{\overline F},{\mathds Q}_\ell)$ takes values in $T({\mathds Q}_\ell)$ for every $\ell$.
The above decompositions give a representation
\[
\Phi\colon T\longrightarrow
\prod_j\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^j_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q}))
\]
such that $\Phi(T)=\operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})$ and, for every $\ell$, the composition
\[
G_F \longrightarrow T({\mathds Q}_\ell)
\xlongrightarrow{\Phi}
\prod_i\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(H^i_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline F},{\mathds Q}_\ell))
\]
is the usual Galois representation on the total cohomology of $X$.
In particular, the algebraic monodromy group of $X$ is connected (for every $\ell$).

Finally, let $U\subset V^2_B(1)$ be the orthogonal complement of $\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}\nolimits(X)_{\mathds Q}=\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}\nolimits(X_{\overline{F}})_{\mathds Q}$.
The CM structure gives
\[
T\simeq \mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits(U)\longrightarrow \mathop{\mathrm{GSpin}}\nolimits(V^2_B(1)).
\]
Since $C^\epsilon$ and $C$ are isomorphic over ${\mathds C}$, they have the same $T$-representation on $H^1_B$.
Thus there exists a $T$-equivariant isomorphism
\[
\theta \colon H^1_B((C^\epsilon)_{{\mathds C}},{\mathds Q})^{\oplus 64} \stackrel{\textstyle\sim}{\smash{\longrightarrow}\rule{0pt}{0.4ex}} \mathop{\mathrm{Cl}}\nolimits(V^2_B(1)).
\]
We set $A\coloneqq (C^\epsilon)^{64}$.
By construction, one can check that $A$, equipped with the isomorphism $\theta$, is a Kuga--Satake abelian variety over $F$ in the sense of \Cref{Definition: Kuga-Satake abelian variety}.
Since $A$ has good reduction at $v$,
the inertia subgroup $I_v$ acts trivially on $H^1_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(A_{\overline F},{\mathds Q}_\ell)$
for $\ell\neq3$.
On the other hand, it acts on $H^3_\mathrm{\acute{e}t}(X_{\overline F},{\mathds Q}_\ell)$ through the nontrivial character $\epsilon|_{I_v}$.
Thus the character in \Cref{Proposition:LLV and Kuga-Satake} is nontrivial.

label: Definition:the integer D_0
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{Definition:the integer D_0}
    We fix a positive integer $D_0$ divisible by $p$, with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item $\Lambda_{B,{\mathds Z}[1/D_0]}\coloneqq \Lambda_B\otimes_{\mathds Z}{\mathds Z}[1/D_0]$ is torsion-free.
\item The schematic closure $\mathcal{G}\subset\mathop{\mathrm{GL}}\nolimits(\Lambda_{B,{\mathds Z}[1/D_0]})$ of $\mathbf{G}$ is a reductive group scheme over ${\mathds Z}[1/D_0]$.
\item Every prime $\ell\nmid D_0$ satisfies $\ell>b_1(X)$ when $X$ is an abelian variety and $\ell > \max_i  b_i(X)$ when $X$ is a hyper-Kähler~ variety.
\item $q-1\in{\mathds Z}[1/D_0]^\times$ and for every geometric Frobenius lift $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q\in W_{F_v}$, any two distinct eigenvalues $a,b$ of $r_v(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q)$ on $H^i_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q})\otimes_{\mathds Q}\overline{{\mathds Q}}$ satisfy
$
a-b\in\overline{{\mathds Z}}[1/D_0]^\times,
$
where $i=1$ if $X$ is an abelian variety and $i$ is arbitrary if $X$ is a hyper-Kähler~ variety.
\item $\rho_v$ extends to a $\mathcal{G}$-valued Weil--Deligne representation of $F_v$ over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}[1/D_0]$:
\[
\rho^{\mathrm{int}}_v=(r^{\mathrm{int}}_v,N^{\mathrm{int}}_v).
\]
Here $\overline{{\mathds Z}}$ is the ring of algebraic integers in $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$.
\end{enumerate}
These conditions can be achieved by taking $D_0$ sufficiently divisible.
head: environment

label: Proposition: ell independence of Weil part of integral MT representation
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Proposition: ell independence of Weil part of integral MT representation}
Let $\ell\nmid D_0$ be a prime.
The representations $(r^{\mathrm{int}}_v)_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$ and $r^{\operatorname{MT},\mathrm{int}}_{\ell,v}$ are $\mathcal{G}(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$-conjugate.
Here $(r^{\mathrm{int}}_v)_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$ denotes the base change of $r^{\mathrm{int}}_v$ along the map $\overline{{\mathds Z}}[1/D_0] \to \overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ induced by $\iota_\ell$.
Moreover, their scheme-theoretic centralizers in $\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$ are smooth over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.
head: environment
labels: Proposition: ell independence of Weil part of integral MT representation

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a geometric Frobenius lift $\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q\in W_{F_v}$, and put
\[
x\coloneqq (r^{\mathrm{int}}_v)_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q),
\quad
y\coloneqq r^{\operatorname{MT},\mathrm{int}}_{\ell,v}(\mathop{\mathrm{Frob}}\nolimits_q).
\]
Their generic fibers are semisimple and $\mathbf{G}(\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell)$-conjugate by rational strong compatibility.
The centralizers of $x$ and $y$ in $\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$ are smooth and contain maximal tori $T_x$ and $T_y$ of $\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$ by \Cref{Lemma: smoothness of Frobenius centralizer}.
Since a maximal torus is its own centralizer, we have $x\in T_x(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$ and $y\in T_y(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$.
By \cite[Theorem~3.2.6]{Conrad2014}, these tori are $\mathcal{G}(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$-conjugate, so we may assume that $x,y\in T(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$ for a common maximal torus $T$.
Their generic fibers then lie in the same orbit with respect to the action of the Weyl group associated with $T$.
The corresponding element in the Weyl group lifts to an element $g \in N_{\mathcal{G}_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}}(T)(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$ since the Weyl group (scheme) is finite \'etale and $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ is strictly henselian.
It follows that $gxg^{-1}=y$.

The images of the inertia subgroup for both representations are central, and rational strong compatibility implies that their restrictions to the inertia subgroup are the same.
It follows that $(r^{\mathrm{int}}_v)_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$ and $r^{\operatorname{MT},\mathrm{int}}_{\ell,v}$ are conjugate by the element $g$.
Their centralizers equal those of $x$ and $y$, respectively, and hence are smooth over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.

label: Proposition: torsion freeness of cohomological monodromy
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Proposition: torsion freeness of cohomological monodromy}
Let $K$ be a finite extension of ${\mathds Q}_p$, and let $X$ be an abelian variety or a hyper-Kähler~ variety over $K$.
Fix integers $i,m,n \geq 0$, and consider the $G_K$-module
\[
H^i_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline K},{\mathds Z}_\ell)^{\otimes m}\otimes_{{\mathds Z}_\ell}
H^i_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline K},{\mathds Z}_\ell)^{\vee, \otimes n}.
\]
For all but finitely many $\ell \neq p$, the monodromy operator $N_\ell$ of the Weil--Deligne representation $\rho_\ell=(r_\ell, N_\ell)$ of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ associated with this $G_K$-module (\Cref{Example: integral Weil-Deligne construction}) has the following property \textup{(t-f)}: For all $j \geq 0$, the cokernel of $(N_\ell)^{j}$ is torsion-free.
head: environment
labels: Proposition: torsion freeness of cohomological monodromy

title: Proof
body_md:
The property \textup{(t-f)} is preserved by duals and tensor products after excluding finitely many further primes.
Indeed, by \cite[Lemma~2.10]{Ito21} and Nakayama's lemma,
\textup{(t-f)} is equivalent to compatibility of the monodromy
filtration with reduction to $\overline{{\mathds F}}_\ell$.
This compatibility is preserved by duals and tensor products,
since the formulas given in \cite[Proposition~(1.6.9)]{WeilII}
remain valid over $\overline{{\mathds F}}_\ell$
outside a finite set of primes depending only on
the ranks of the underlying modules.
Thus it suffices to consider the Weil--Deligne representation $\rho_\ell=(r_\ell, N_\ell)$ of $K$ over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ associated with $H^i_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline K},{\mathds Z}_\ell)$.
If $X$ is an abelian variety, then the assertion is proved in \cite{Ito21}; more precisely, this follows from \cite[Theorem~3.7 and Proposition~3.10(ii)]{Ito21}.
We assume that $X$ is a hyper-Kähler~ variety over $K$.
If $i=2$, then this again follows from \cite{Ito21}.
We shall deduce the general case from this case.

We choose an embedding $K \hookrightarrow {\mathds C}$ and let $\mathbf{G}\coloneqq \operatorname{MT}(X_{\mathds C})$.
We may assume that $K=K^c$ and obtain the representation $\phi^{\operatorname{MT}}_\ell \colon G_K \to \mathbf{G}({\mathds Q}_\ell)$ for all $\ell$ as in \Cref{Subsection:MT-WD representation}.
By \Cref{lem:weighted tensor generation}, $H^i_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q})^{\otimes2}$ is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of $H^2_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q})^{\otimes a} \otimes H^2_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q})^{\vee, \otimes b}$ for some $a, b$ as a $\mathbf{G}$-representation.
From this, we see that $H^i_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline K},{\mathds Z}_\ell)^{\otimes2}$ is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of $H^2_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline K},{\mathds Z}_\ell)^{\otimes a} \otimes H^2_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline K},{\mathds Z}_\ell)^{\vee, \otimes b}$ as a $G_K$-module for all but finitely many $\ell \neq p$.
It follows that $\rho_\ell^{\otimes 2}$ satisfies property \textup{(t-f)}.
Finally, property \textup{(t-f)} can be detected on tensor squares
for sufficiently large $\ell$.
Indeed, the monodromy filtration on a tensor square is the
tensor product filtration, both in characteristic zero and,
for all but finitely many $\ell$, after reduction to
$\overline{{\mathds F}}_\ell$.
Since a filtration is determined by its tensor square,
compatibility of the monodromy filtration with reduction
for $\rho_\ell^{\otimes2}$ implies the same compatibility
for $\rho_\ell$.
Thus $\rho_\ell$ also has property \textup{(t-f)}.
This completes the proof.

label: Proposition: integral purity of MT representations
title: Proposition
head: environment
labels: Proposition: integral purity of MT representations

title: Proof
body_md:
We want to apply \Cref{Lemma: sufficient criterion for integral purity}.
By the preceding results (and the corresponding known results for abelian varieties), the generic fibers are Frobenius semisimple and pure with respect to $\mu$.
Condition (d) implies that the Frobenius-weight cocharacters are defined over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ for every $\ell \nmid D_0$.
Moreover, the scheme-theoretic centralizers of 
the corresponding actions of $W_{F_v}$ are smooth over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$ by \Cref{Proposition: ell independence of Weil part of integral MT representation}.
Thus conditions \textup{(1)--(3)} of \Cref{Definition:integral G-valued purity} hold.

Let $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits\coloneqq  \mathop{\mathrm{Lie}}\nolimits(\mathcal{G})$.
Since $\rho_v$ is defined over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$, it is easy to see that there exists a positive integer $D$ divisible by $D_0$, such that, for every prime $\ell\nmid D$, the isotypic decomposition of $\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Q}}_\ell}$ for the action of $r^{\mathrm{int}}_v(W_{F_v})$ is defined over $\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell$.
By \Cref{Proposition: ell independence of Weil part of integral MT representation}, the same holds for $r^{\operatorname{MT},\mathrm{int}}_{\ell,v}$.

It remains to show that for all but finitely many $\ell$, the cokernels of
\[
d_1 \colon \mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell} \longrightarrow \mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}, \quad Y \mapsto [Y, N^{\mathrm{int}}_v]
\]
and
\[
d_2 \colon \mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell} \longrightarrow \mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}, \quad Y \mapsto [Y, N^{\operatorname{MT}, \mathrm{int}}_{\ell, v}]
\]
are torsion-free.
Since $\rho_v$ is defined over $\overline{{\mathds Q}}$, one can easily check the assertion for $d_1$.
For $d_2$, we note that
the natural
$\mathbf{G}$-equivariant inclusion
\[
\mathop{\mathfrak{g}}\nolimits_{\mathds Q}\hookrightarrow
\bigoplus_i\mathop{\mathrm{End}}\nolimits(H^i_B(X_{\mathds C},{\mathds Q}))
\]
splits since $\mathbf{G}$ is reductive.
After enlarging $D$, we may assume that the inclusion and splitting extend
over ${\mathds Z}[1/D]$.
Under the \'etale--Betti comparison, this splitting is also $G_{F_v}$-equivariant.
Now \Cref{Proposition: torsion freeness of cohomological monodromy} implies that after enlarging $D$ further, the cokernel of $d_2$ is torsion-free for every $\ell \nmid D$.

All the hypotheses of \Cref{Lemma: sufficient criterion for integral purity} are now satisfied for both representations.

label: Theorem:integral compatibility for HK
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{Proposition: integral purity of MT representations}, we may choose $D$ divisible by $D_0$ such that both representations are pure with respect to $\mu$ for every $\ell \nmid D$.
Their generic fibers are Frobenius semisimple, and the representations $(r^{\mathrm{int}}_v)_{\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell}$ and $r^{\operatorname{MT},\mathrm{int}}_{\ell,v}$ are $\mathcal{G}(\overline{{\mathds Z}}_\ell)$-conjugate by \Cref{Proposition: ell independence of Weil part of integral MT representation}.
The assertion therefore follows from \Cref{Proposition:uniqueness of monodromy operator integral case}.
